extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, administrators, and NIH grantee/award applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH policy updates, resources, and reminders relevant to preparing and submitting NIH grant applications and managing awards. Includes pointers to new formats, policy changes, and interpretation of review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of research models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential (e.g., new approach methodologies, NAMs). Choose models that best address the hypothesis and translational aims rather than defaulting to a particular system; prioritize scientific soundness and human relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has a 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure covering key features and application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the overview to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time (JIT) requests. Be aware that PF5 applications have a specific format and post-review administrative splitting may occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH. Consult the new resource to ensure compliance with current required elements and formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research is emphasized; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture that values replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications, awards, and institutional practices should incorporate plans or elements that promote replication and reproducibility. NIH launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative and highlighted a topic to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts—applicants should describe how their work supports reliability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that a 'competitive but not discussed' designation does not necessarily mean an application is weak; it reflects procedural cutoffs used during the modified review process. Reviewers and applicants should account for how cohort cutoffs and centralized procedures can affect discussion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) as of March 2025; NIH reports consolidation is strengthening efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that peer review processes, timing, and possibly study section composition/rubrics may be affected by centralization. Monitor NIH guidance and communications for any procedural changes that could affect submission strategy or expectations about review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the NIH Data Book for up-to-date fiscal and program data
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiscal year 2025 data in the NIH Data Book are being rolled out to ensure users have access to the most recent information available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NIH Data Book for current fiscal and programmatic statistics that may inform application context, budgeting, and understanding of funding patterns; check for updates as new data are released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of NIH Seed Fund and small business opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Small Business Program (Seed Fund) has been reinstated and is back in action for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses and entrepreneurs should look for solicitations, eligibility criteria, and application details related to the Seed Fund and other small business programs; consider these opportunities during planning and proposal development.
